### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb7b09d4d28ea0a878dea993d2fa5cc9226bc92f`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb7b09d4d28ea0a878dea993d2fa5cc9226bc92f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `443fa7aab24953334c61b6fbdae07bed4115da28` — the merge of head `4aa292ec54eba99d90e6700717ea31361ed41426` into base `eb7b09d4d28ea0a878dea993d2fa5cc9226bc92f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 443fa7aab24953334c61b6fbdae07bed4115da28 && git checkout 443fa7aab24953334c61b6fbdae07bed4115da28
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eb7b09d4d28ea0a878dea993d2fa5cc9226bc92f 4aa292ec54eba99d90e6700717ea31361ed41426 && git checkout -B drift-repro eb7b09d4d28ea0a878dea993d2fa5cc9226bc92f && git merge --no-ff 4aa292ec54eba99d90e6700717ea31361ed41426

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb7b09d4d28ea0a878dea993d2fa5cc9226bc92f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eb7b09d4d28ea0a878dea993d2fa5cc9226bc92f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzfWpJ96QY9T7d8DvFg

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-18T01:06Z

Head-sha: 4aa292ec54eba99d90e6700717ea31361ed41426
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #35048 (os-dev report 6965784090).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Fixes #35048`, base `main`. Three paths, +106/-11:
- `RecordedDriver` in `runner/driver.ts`;
- two cases in `orchestrate.test.ts`;
- a `@objectstack/scenarios` patch changeset.

Not governed. `CREATING_TOOLS` is module-private, and `createdIdOf` stays unexported (its arity changed). So no export moves and no served MCP surface moves, and `Clause-②: no` holds under the seat's ruling. The replay's verdict on such a turn does move, from not measured to graded, which is the fix itself.

**CI.** It was still running when I read it (15 pending, nothing failed). This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

**The holder matches the real answer.** `createdIdOf(tool, output)` reads `result.id` for `run_action`, and the top-level `id` for `create_record`. The runtime's `run_action` answer is `{ ok: true, action, objectName, recordId?, result }`, with `result` being what the action body returned (`domains/mcp.ts:2285`). So an action that creates a row and returns it names that row at `result.id`. A non-object `result`, or one with no string `id`, yields `undefined`, so no mapping is made.

**The guard.** The remap runs only for a `CREATING_TOOLS` write recorded as `applied`, and only when both ids are present and differ. That leaves these cases harmless:
- an action that answers the id of a row it only updated. A seeded row keeps the card's id on both runs, so `was === now` and nothing is mapped. A row the run created earlier maps to the mapping it already has.
- a refused or unanswered write. That path is unchanged and handled by the faithfulness check above it.

**Pins and ablation.**
- **The pin.** A `run_action`'s `result.id` is remapped into the same turn's submit and into a later turn's `update_record`.
- **The control.** `create_record`'s top-level id is still remapped, into a later `update_record` and a later `run_action`.
- **The ablation.** Reverting the holder, and separately the guard, each turns the pin red with `ReplayNotFaithfulError` (`RECORD_NOT_FOUND` on replay).

**Live replay.** On the iteration-2 recording, Run-operations goes from 2/2 with 4 not measured to 2/3 with 3 not measured. `file_and_submit_from_text` is now graded, and fails on the build's own `HOOK_ABORTED` submit (status `draft` against `submitted`). That is a real finding about the build that the replay used to hide, which is what #34996 needed unblocked.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. An action whose body creates several rows and returns only one id (or an array) maps only that one, or none. No card does this today. If one does, the turn reads not faithful again, loudly, and does not mis-grade. Not owed.

Next: o3-F (2) lands once the three aggregates are green. No seat L2 is owed. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
